titleFormatted.en: Add activity monitor for [[device]], capability [[capability]], threshold [[threshold]] W, name [[name]]

hint.en: Continuity window and minimum confirmation start at 0 (off) here — tune them later with "Update activity monitor" if you notice fragmented or noisy cycles.
Leave blank to use measure_power. Other relevant capabilities on this device (current, energy, voltage) are detected and tracked automatically — no need to add them here.

For a fire-and-forget occurrence with no start/end pair — a doorbell press, a single motion pulse, a button click. Just tallies how many times it happened, no duration or energy. Run once to set it up (or wire it to a native trigger — running it again on the same name updates the existing counter instead of duplicating it), then use "Log binary event" wherever the real occurrence happens.
Pick an existing counter to update it, or type a new name and pick "Create new" to make one.

titleFormatted.en: Add state monitor for [[device]], capability [[capability]], label when true [[true_label]], label when false [[false_label]], name [[name]]

hint.en: For a boolean capability with no meaningful numeric threshold — a door, a presence sensor, an on/off switch. Tracks time spent in BOTH states — no need to guess which raw value (true/false) means what, just name them. Not for power monitoring — use "Add activity monitor" for that.
Only boolean capabilities on this device are shown (contact, motion, on/off, etc.).

What the raw value true means for this device — check its current value against its current physical state if unsure. Used only for display, doesn't affect what gets tracked (both states are always tracked).

hint.en: Leave blank to use measure_voltage. Pick a phase-specific capability here if the device exposes one.
Readings during this window after creating the monitor only establish the reference and never fire an isolated event — avoids false alarms from an anomalous first reading.

titleFormatted.en: Get binary event statistics for [[counter]], period: [[period]]

hint.en: Call this from whatever Flow already reacts to the real occurrence (a native trigger — contact alarm, motion, button). The message token is built from the wording configured for this counter in Settings — no message field needed here.

Wipes cycles, history and live state (e.g. after fixing a monitor that was recording wrong data) — keeps the monitor itself, its device, capability, threshold and settings. To remove the monitor entirely instead, use "Remove activity monitor".
Wipes the count and history — keeps the counter itself and its message wording. To remove the counter entirely instead, use "Remove binary counter".
Wipes sessions, history and live state — keeps the monitor itself, its device, capability and settings. To remove the monitor entirely instead, use "Remove state monitor".

Wipes readings, events and live state (e.g. after fixing a monitor that was bound to the wrong capability) — keeps the monitor itself, its device, capability, voltage range and message wording. To remove the monitor entirely instead, use "Remove voltage monitor".

For an on/off-only device (a pump, a device with no reliable standby signal) — creates the monitor on first run if it doesn't exist yet, then starts it, in one step. Meant to be driven by a native "Power becomes greater than X" trigger (or any other Flow logic) instead of this app's own threshold engine. The resulting monitor never decides active/standby on its own — only this card and "Stop monitoring device" do.

Closes the cycle started by "Start monitoring device" for this device — fires "Activity finished" with duration, energy and the rest of the usual tokens. Fails if no monitor exists yet for this device; run "Start monitoring device" first.
